title: Romans Bible Quiz - Chapter 11
description: Ten questions on Romans 11: the remnant of grace, Elijah's complaint, the grafted wild olive, and the unsearchable judgments of God.

questions.text: Of which tribe does the writer say he is?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:1 says he also is an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

questions.text: How many men did God say he had reserved for himself who had not bowed the knee to Baal?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:4 says God answers Elijah that he has reserved for himself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.

questions.text: According to what is there a remnant at this present time?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:5 says that even so at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

questions.text: What does the quotation say God gave them?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:8 quotes that God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, to this very day.

questions.text: To whom has salvation come by their fall?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:11 says that by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.

answers.text: To the kings of the earth

questions.text: What is the person who was grafted in among the branches called?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:17 says that some of the branches were broken off and that you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them.

questions.text: What does the text say about the root and the one who boasts?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:18 says not to boast over the branches, because it is not you who support the root, but the root supports you.

answers.text: The root and the branches support each other

questions.text: Why were the branches broken off, according to the text?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:20 says that by their unbelief they were broken off, and that you stand by your faith.

answers.text: By the hardness of the soil
By the wrath of the rulers

questions.text: What has happened to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:25 says the writer does not want them ignorant of this mystery, that a partial hardening has happened to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in.

questions.text: What does the text say about the gifts and the calling of God?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:29 says that the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

answers.text: They are given only to the strong
They last for a single generation
